subtype: Approach: leaving it to the last week [Pitfall]
passage: Yusuf's group had three weeks to build a model water purifier and assumed there was plenty of time. They met once, in the first week, to choose a design, and never fixed dates. In week three, Ishita's family left for a wedding in another city and another member came down with a fever, so by Wednesday only Yusuf and one other were left. The exhibition was on Friday. On Thursday night Yusuf glued the tubes while Ishita, back late, painted the base. The label was crooked and one tube leaked. On Friday a judge asked how the filter worked, and Yusuf gave a half answer while water dripped onto the table. Ishita looked at her shoes.

qa.q: How often did the group meet in the first three weeks?
qa.a: The group met only once, in the first week.

qa.q: What might Yusuf be feeling as water dripped while the judge waited?
qa.a: Yusuf is probably embarrassed and frustrated, giving a half answer while the leak shows the rush.

qa.q: What could the group have done at the start, and why?
qa.a: They could have set dates for each stage and short check-ins, because a plan with dates shows problems early, before absences hit.

qa.q: How might Ishita see the finished model?
qa.a: Ishita likely feels guilty and awkward, having missed part of the work, which is why Ishita looked at the shoes.

grounding: The group assumes there is plenty of time and meets only once, and in the final week two members are absent and the model is finished in a rush with obvious flaws.
